content:
You can finish a stack of courses and still be unready to preach, lead a meeting, or sit with a hurting person. You can also work hard in a church and never hear an honest review of what you did. Training helps when it matches a gap you and your sending leaders can name.

This reference compares six formats by supervision, practice, feedback, time, and cost. It does not rank schools, networks, or events, and it does not set a required sequence before you plant. Finishing a course is not proof that you are ready. Readiness is a judgment people make about your life and your work. A certificate cannot make that judgment, and neither can this Wiki or Everyfield.

---

## Name the gap first

Start with what you cannot yet do. Ask the leaders who would send you what they want to see you practice, and write it down. A learning need names the skill or knowledge, and names who could watch you try it.

Common gaps, not a required list:

- You have not preached a full sermon to a congregation.
- You have not led a team through a disagreement.
- You do not yet know how a church handles money, children, or membership.
- You have ideas about a city and no practiced way of meeting people there.

If the question is calling or character, a class will not settle it. People who know you have to speak to that. Software does not judge calling, character, fitness, or spiritual health. Everyfield does not certify planters or gate this training.

<Callout type="tip">
Write one sentence per need. "I need practice in this, with someone who will tell me what they saw." No watcher, no plan.
</Callout>

<Callout type="scripture">
*"And the things which you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who will be able to teach others also."* — 2 Timothy 2:2 (LSB)
</Callout>

What you learn is for passing on. Watched practice belongs in the plan, not only notes from a lecture.

---

## How the formats differ

Match the gap to the format. This is a comparison, not a ranking. Names below describe a format. They are not a list to join. Time and price change, so confirm both before you register.

### Supervised ministry

A named supervisor reviews real church assignments for a length you set together. Ask about pay. Weak if you only need a fast survey.

### Residency

Senior leaders mentor an employed role you own. Ask about length and pay. One published model is at least two years and includes employment. Too much if you need one narrow skill.

### Short course or intensive

An instructor comments on assignments packed into days or weeks. Schools publish tuition. A church course may not. Ask. Not months of supervised ministry.

### Conference

Ideas and new people, then you leave. No review of your own work after that. Ticket, plus travel if you go. Confirm the price.

### Coaching

Agreed questions, work between meetings, cost in the agreement. The coach does not watch you preach or lead unless you ask.

### Self-study

Your pace. Mostly books and time. No reviewer unless you add one. Fit for knowledge you can test, not for a skill someone should watch.

<Callout type="important">
Confirm time and cost with the church or school before you register. A page or a conversation from last season is not a promise.
</Callout>

---

## Supervised ministry and residencies

Supervised ministry puts you in a real setting to do the kind of work you hope to take on. For a Master of Divinity, the Commission on Accrediting of the Association of Theological Schools requires supervised practical experiences, such as a practicum or internship, in a fitting setting, for long enough, under supervisors who are qualified and regularly evaluated. That rule governs degree programs. It is not a church-planting credential. Outside a school, look for the same shape.

An apprenticeship is that shape in a church. You take assigned work, someone watches, and you hear what they saw. Acts 29 names apprenticeships and residencies as its preparation stage, then assessment and coaching later. That is one network's process. This Wiki does not adopt that sequence, or any other, as the path you must walk.

Made to Flourish, which helps churches start residencies, describes a resident who is given responsibility, mentored by senior leaders, and employed in a local church. Its model lasts a minimum of two years, after a degree or during one. Do not treat two years or employment as the rule everywhere. Ask what you will do each week and when someone will tell you what they saw. A title without a named supervisor is a job, not training.

---

## Short courses and conferences

Accreditors let a school count a credit hour on the usual weekly pattern, or as the equivalent amount of work over a different period of time. A short course can still be real work. It is still mostly instruction and assignments, not months of watched ministry.

A conference is a gathering. Exponential describes one ticket as access to main sessions, speakers, selected workshops, and interviews. Use it to surface a learning need or meet a person. It will not supervise your next sermon. Put anything you want to keep into the plan, or let it go.

Some outside planter courses use the words boot camp for a class before you plant. In this Wiki, Boot Camp is different. It is intensive discipleship for emerging leaders in the church you are planting. Read [Boot Camp Overview](/wiki/training/boot-camp-overview) before you use the term with your team. Launch Team training starts after a launch date is set and prepares the team for Launch Sunday. See [Training Programs Overview](/wiki/training/training-programs-overview). An outside planter course is neither of those, even if a brochure borrows the words.

<Callout type="warning">
Course completion is not proof of readiness. A certificate, a finished module, or a conference badge does not show that you can pastor a people. Sending leaders who know your life and your work make that judgment. A provider cannot make it for them.
</Callout>

---

## Coaching and self-study

Coaching is a relationship, not a syllabus. The International Coaching Federation defines coaching as partnering with clients in a thought-provoking and creative process that inspires them to maximize their personal and professional potential. In planting, use it for questions, a check on what you said you would do, and help with a decision. Do not assume the coach will watch you preach or lead unless you agree on that. How to find a person is in [Finding a Coach/Mentor](/wiki/discovery/finding-a-coach-mentor).

Self-study is reading, listening, and writing on your own. It fits a knowledge gap you can test, such as a book of the Bible or a policy you must explain. Accredited schools may allow independent study, but not as an entire degree, and they still expect a qualified instructor and evaluation of the work. Copy that limit. Self-study can fill a gap. It cannot be the whole plan for work someone should watch.

---

## Build one plan

You and your sending leaders turn the needs into one plan. Choosing by need can leave you with unrelated courses. Reviewing the whole plan is how you avoid that.

For each need:

- [ ] Name the gap in one sentence.
- [ ] Pick the format that supplies the missing practice, teaching, or feedback.
- [ ] Name the person who will watch the work or review it with you.
- [ ] Set a date to look at the work together before you register.
- [ ] Write what finished means in observed practice, not in attendance.

Three needs with a watcher beat eight registrations with none. Prior experience covers a need only when someone who saw the work will say so. A past title does not. If two formats both touch the gap, pick more watched practice for a skill and clearer teaching for a knowledge gap.

---

## Who reviews the plan

Someone has to read the plan as one piece. Before you commit money or a long stretch of time, ask:

- The Senior Pastor of your sending church, or the leaders who would actually send you
- A coach or mentor who will still be in the work with you, if you have one
- You, checked against the gaps you wrote, not against a brochure

They should be able to say whether each gap has fitting teaching or practice, who gives feedback, what you will look at when the block ends, and what you are leaving out on purpose.

Everyfield does not review this plan, approve it, or treat it as a credential. A network assessment, if you enter one, is that network's process. It does not replace your sending leaders. This Wiki does not require it.

<Callout type="insight">
Choosing by learning need works only if someone you trust can say the pieces add up. A menu of courses is not a plan.
</Callout>

---

## Mistakes that waste the year

- Signing up because a brochure listed a sequence, with no named gap.
- Treating a conference as supervised ministry.
- Calling an outside planter course Boot Camp.
- Letting a certificate stand in for a judgment your sending leaders never made.
- Studying alone what you needed someone to watch.
- Asking software, a course, or this article whether you are called or ready.

When the plan is reviewed, put the next practice on the calendar. Then do the work where someone can see it.

title: Training Options for Planters

sources.claim: 2 Timothy 2:2, Legacy Standard Bible, quoted in the scripture callout.
sources.quote: And the things which you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.

sources.claim: A Master of Divinity requires supervised practical experiences of sufficient duration under qualified, regularly evaluated supervisors. This is a degree-program standard, not a church-planting credential.
sources.quote: The Master of Divinity degree requires supervised practical experiences (e.g., practicum or internship) in areas related to the student’s vocational calling in order to achieve the learning outcomes of the degree program. These experiences are in settings that are appropriately chosen, well suited to the experience needed, and of sufficient duration. These experiences are also supervised by those who are appropriately qualified, professionally developed, and regularly evaluated.

sources.claim: Accredited schools may offer independent study, but not as an entire degree, and degree courses still require qualified instructors and evaluation of student work.
sources.quote: The school may offer individualized instruction, such as independent studies or individualized field education, provided it meets the first two components and is limited to meeting appropriate student needs or particular degree program requirements, but not an entire degree

sources.claim: Those degree-course components include qualified instructors and evaluation of student work.
sources.quote: initiate substantive, course-related interactions with students, including evaluating student work

sources.claim: Schools must state tuition and fee charges publicly.
sources.quote: The school states publicly, follows consistently, and reviews regularly various policies for its degree programs, including tuition and fee charges

sources.claim: A credit hour may be the equivalent amount of work over a different period of time, so a compressed course can still be real student work.
sources.quote: or the equivalent amount of work over a different period of time

sources.quote: Residents are given responsibility, mentored by senior leaders, and prepared for life-long faithfulness in ministry.

sources.claim: That organization's published residency model includes pastoral employment and lasts a minimum of two years, after graduation or during degree completion. The article does not treat those terms as universal.
sources.quote: Involves pastoral employment for the resident

Made to Flourish places that residency after graduation or during degree completion, and in a local church.
sources.quote: Occurs after graduation or during degree completion

sources.quote: Train through apprenticeships and residencies that form both theology and leadership.

sources.claim: Acts 29 lists assessment and coaching as a later step in its own process, not as a Wiki requirement.
sources.quote: Enter assessment, receive coaching, access resources, and plant within a network built to multiply.

sources.quote: our digital ticket includes online access to the main sessions including our powerful worship and impactful speakers, select workshops, additional equipping content, and exclusive speaker interviews.

rulings: Bryan ruled B12 = Option A: "Choose by learning need" (2026-10-26).
Wording: no fees, stipends, or calendar dates in the body. Cost is described by type, and the reader is told to confirm current terms, because published prices go stale.

Wording: Acts 29, Made to Flourish, Exponential, the ATS Commission on Accrediting, and the International Coaching Federation are named only to define a format or a standard. They are not a recommended list, and no network sequence is adopted.

Wording: outside planter courses that use the words boot camp are distinguished from the Wiki Boot Camp in training/boot-camp-overview and from Launch Team training in training/training-programs-overview.
Wording: finished means observed practice, not attendance, so course completion is not treated as proof of readiness.
